headlines.article_text: Blue Origin pushes launch to 2027 as it races to rebuild launch pad Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin has delayed its New Glenn return to flight to January 2027, after previously targeting a launch by the end of this year. Blue Origin CEO Dave Limp said the company has moved swiftly to repair a launchpad that was damaged by the New Glenn explosion in May, but the work hasn't been easy. "This small adjustment doesn't diminish what we've accomplished or the importance of the work still ahead," Limp said. A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket is prepared for launch at the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Cape Canaveral, Florida, U.S., April 18, 2026. Joe Skipper | Reuters Jeff Bezos ' Blue Origin has delayed a return to flight for its flagship New Glenn rocket to January 2027, later than its earlier target of the end of this year, as it rushes to recover from a major explosion in May. Blue Origin CEO Dave Limp told employees in a memo Wednesday that the company's launch timing slipped as a result of delays with reconstructing its Cape Canaveral launch pad, including bad weather over the summer. "This small adjustment doesn't diminish what we've accomplished or the importance of the work still ahead," Limp wrote in the memo, which was viewed by CNBC. "Returning New Glenn to flight remains our top priority — it's worth it." Tune in at 4:45 p.m. ET as Blue Origin CEO Dave Limp joins CNBC TV exclusively. Watch in real time on CNBC+ or the CNBC Pro stream. The Financial Times earlier reported the memo. The January 2027 timeframe is about 10 days later than Blue Origin's earlier launch target, a source familiar with the matter told CNBC. The New Glenn explosion in May, which occurred during a hot-fire test, badly damaged Blue Origin's Florida launchpad. The company was slated to deploy 48 satellites for Amazon 's Leo internet-from-space service just a few days later. Since then, the company has moved swiftly to repair the launch facility and reworked its pad configuration. Bezos told Fox News last month that the company was still expecting New Glenn to fly again in December. Limp said Blue Origin has made great progress on the recovery, but he noted that "rebuilding at this pace hasn't been easy." "Your collective work on our return to flight has been nothing short of remarkable," Limp wrote. "In just six months, Team Blue has accomplished what many thought would take years." The mishap was inconveniently timed, as Blue Origin has been working to ramp up its launch cadence in an effort to compete with its chief rival, Elon Musk 's SpaceX , for commercial and government customers. The New Glenn delays have hampered Amazon's Leo constellation buildout, for which it relies on Blue Origin for a portion of its launches. Amazon has turned to other providers including United Launch Alliance and Arianespace in the interim, especially as SpaceX has phased out Falcon 9 launches to prioritize testing its enormous Starship rocket. NASA has also tapped Blue Origin for several contracts in the agency's Artemis return-to-the-moon program, including a lunar lander. headlines.title: Stocks making the biggest moves midday: Micron, Tesla, Tripadvisor, AppLovin, Nvidia & more
headlines.summary: Here are some of the companies making headlines in midday trading.
headlines.article_text: Stocks making the biggest moves midday: MU, TSLA, TRIP, APP, NVDA Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Here are some of the companies making headlines in midday trading. Artificial intelligence infrastructure – Companies tied to the AI data center build-out saw shares tank, contributing to the Nasdaq Composite's slide into a correction. The iShares A.I. Innovation and Tech Active ETF (BAI) shed 10%. Photonics play Lumentum slid 14%, HVAC service provider Comfort Systems lost 10%, CoreWeave tumbled 12%, Corning dropped 13% and nVent Electric slid more than 12%. Semiconductors – Traders backed away from chips as the tech sector sold off hard Thursday. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) was last down more than 9%. Fabless semiconductor stock Astera Labs dropped 15%, while AMD shed 14%. Nvidia and Broadcom each lost almost 7%. Memory chip stocks Micron fell almost 13% while SanDisk plunged 20%. Tripadvisor – Shares of the travel platform operator plummeted 22% on the back of a leadership shakeup and disappointing guidance. Tripadvisor CEO Matt Goldberg will leave the platform, as will finance chief Michael Noonan. Goldberg will remain as CEO through Feb. 16, while Noonan will continue in his role through Dec. 31. Separately, TripAdvisor forecast a fourth-quarter sequential revenue decline in the low teens. Motorola Solutions – The security tech company jumped 5% on the back of a guidance raise for the full year. Motorola anticipates adjusted earnings of $17.94 to $17.99 per share on revenue of about $13.05 billion. That compares to the FactSet consensus call for $17.71 per share and revenue of $12.97 billion. EPAM Systems – The software company soared 22% after raising earnings guidance for the full year. EPAM sees adjusted earnings of $13.23 to $13.31 per share, up from an earlier $13.08 to $13.24 per share and ahead of the FactSet consensus estimate for $13.15. The board also approved a $1.5 billion increase in a buyback authorization. Tesla , SpaceX – Shares of Elon Musk's companies slid for a second day as traders dumped tech stocks and grew skeptical of the artificial intelligence trade. Democrats' midterm victories in Texas, including Gina Hinojosa's win in the gubernatorial race, spurred worries that there could be a slowdown in the AI build-out effort in the state. Tesla tumbled 11%, while SpaceX dropped 9%. Corpay — The corporate spending and payments manager rallied 8% after reporting third-quarter results that beat expectations. Corpay earned $7.54 per share, excluding certain items, on revenue of $1.38 billion. Analysts polled by FactSet expected a profit of $7.20 per share on revenue of $1.36 billion. The company also hiked its full-year outlook for adjusted EBITDA. Tapestry — Shares gained 6% after the luxury fashion company raised its full-year outlook. On a non-GAAP basis, the company expects $8.25 to $8.35 in earnings per share and $8.5 billion to $8.6 billion in revenue for fiscal 2027. Unity Software — Shares of the game development company surged 11% following blowout results. Unity Software posted third-quarter earnings of 25 cents per share on revenue of $622 million. Analysts surveyed by LSEG had expected per-share earnings of 5 cents on revenue of $567 million. Qualcomm — The chipmaker plunged 11% after posting a slight earnings beat in its fiscal fourth-quarter financial report . Qualcomm sees adjusted earnings of $2.15 to $2.35 per share in the current quarter, while analysts polled by FactSet were estimating $2.26 per share. AppLovin — Shares rallied 26% following stronger-than-expected third-quarter results. The software company known for mobile game advertising posted adjusted EBITDA of $1.84 billion, more than the FactSet consensus estimate of $1.73 billion. Revenue of $2.18 billion topped analysts call of $2.07 billion. Expedia — The online booking company slid more than 13% after issuing mostly weaker-than-expected guidance for the current quarter. Expedia sees revenue between $3.69 billion and $3.75 billion in the fourth quarter, but analysts polled by FactSet on average estimated $3.74 billion. Arm Holdings — The designer of central processing units dropped 12% after a strong earnings report. The U.K. company reported adjusted earnings of 52 cents per share, besting the LSEG consensus estimate of 47 cents. Cava — The restaurant chain tumbled 9% after third-quarter results missed expectations. Earnings of 11 cents a share were short of the LSEG consensus estimate of 12 cents. Cava posted revenue of $356 million while analysts expected $359 million. Wolfspeed – The semiconductor manufacturer fell 14% after posting a wider-than-expected loss in the fiscal first quarter. Wolfspeed's adjusted loss of $2.03 per share compared with the FactSet consensus estimate for a $1.99 per share loss. Figma — The software stock dropped 15% after the cloud-based design platform posted third-quarter results that bested expectations. Figma posted adjusted earnings of 10 cents a share on revenue of $391 million, while the LSEG consensus called for 5 cents a share and $376 million. Snap – The social media stock tumbled 15% following third-quarter revenue of $1.72 billion that narrowly missed the LSEG consensus estimate of $1.73 billion. Global daily active users of 495 million also trailed StreetAccount consensus expectations 499 million. Dutch Bros — The coffee chain tumbled 22% after Dutch Bros cut its full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to at least $380 million from a previous range of $385 million to $390 million. Same-store sales in the third quarter were weaker than expected at 4.4%, versus the StreetAccount consensus estimate of 4.6%. Fastly – Shares of the edge cloud platform tumbled 25%, though earnings and revenue in the third quarter topped estimates, as did guidance for the current quarter. The company announced Scott Lovett, president of Go To Market, will retire in 2027. — CNBC's Nick Wells, Ananya Chetia, Contessa Brewer, Davis Giangiulio, Fred Imbert, Paulina Likos and Darla Mercado contributed reporting.

Daniel Heuer | Bloomberg | Getty Images Senate Democrats are gearing up to investigate JPMorgan Chase 's banking relationship with the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein once they take control of Congress early next year. Democratic staffers on the Senate Finance Committee intend to home in on how high-ranking executives at JPMorgan handled Epstein, a source familiar with the panel's thinking told CNBC on Thursday. The person spoke on condition of anonymity because the probe of the nation's biggest bank has not been announced. The Finance Committee is likely to be chaired beginning in January by Sen. Ron Wyden , an Oregon Democrat who currently is the panel's ranking member. Wyden has made clear he plans to make full use of the subpoena powers that committee majorities wield. Democratic staffers aim to focus in particular on decisions about Epstein made by Mary Callahan Erdoes, the CEO of JPMorgan's asset and wealth management division, the source said. JPMorgan declined to comment. The bank has previously said it regrets any association with Epstein but that it did not assist him in committing crimes. In a 2023 deposition , Erdoes said she was aware as early as 2006 that Epstein was accused of paying cash to have underage girls brought to his home. Epstein had been a client of the bank since 1998. The backlash may reach beyond one billionaire Analysis: The Democrats have one chance to extract concessions from Trump. Markets will hate it Epstein became a registered sex offender after pleading guilty in 2008 in Florida to a state criminal charge of procuring an underage girl for prostitution. JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon in his own, later deposition in 2023, said Erdoes had authority to cut off Epstein as a client. She did not take that step until 2013. Epstein, a former friend of President Donald Trump , ex-President Bill Clinton and many other high-profile people, died in a jailhouse suicide in August 2019, weeks after being arrested on federal child sex trafficking charges. Mary Callahan Erdoes, J.P. Morgan Asset & Wealth Management CEO, speaking at CNBC's Delivering Alpha event in New York on Nov. 13th, 2025. Adam Jeffery | CNBC A lawyer for the U.S. Virgin Islands told a federal judge in New York in 2023 that JPMorgan "was a full-service bank for Jeffrey Epstein's sex trafficking," and that it waited until after he killed himself to notify the Treasury Department of $1 billion in suspicious transactions related to trafficking by Epstein. "This was a CYA [cover your a--] reporting after 16 years of all of the monies flowing in his JPMorgan accounts after he was dead," the lawyer, Mimi Liu, said. JPMorgan has blamed former investment banking chief Jes Staley for concealing or failing to report criminal activity related to Epstein, with whom he had a close relationship. Staley, who left JPMorgan in 2013 and later became CEO of Barclays before stepping down in 2021, has denied knowledge of Epstein's crimes. House Oversight Chair James Comer, R-Ky., after a closed-door interview with Staley in July, said that the former executive had encouraged JPMorgan to keep Epstein as a client. In mid-2023, JPMorgan agreed to a $290 million settlement with victims of Epstein without admitting wrongdoing. That same year, JPMorgan agreed to pay $75 million to settle a separate lawsuit by the U.S. Virgin Islands alleging that the bank facilitated and benefited from the sex trafficking of young women by Epstein. In August, Wyden released a report accusing top officials at multiple banks of "looking the other way" as Epstein moved hundreds of millions of dollars to finance a yearslong sex trafficking operation. "The report exposes how top bankers shielded Epstein from federal scrutiny by delaying the reporting of Epstein's suspicious financial activity to the U.S. government, likely in violation of federal anti-money-laundering laws," Wyden's office said in a statement that month. "It includes new details about the extent of suspicious activity reported by Deutsche Bank after Epstein's death, new details from bank reports filed about suspicious transfers to Epstein through accounts at Bank of America, and names top officials at JPMorgan Chase and other banks who were responsible for reporting Epstein's shady activities to the government but instead protected Epstein in order to gain access to Leon Black and other billionaires." Black, former CEO of Apollo Global Management, was revealed to have paid Epstein $158 million for financial advice in the years after his 2008 conviction. In September, Black sued the House oversight panel, seeking to block subpoenas it had issued him for his testimony and for documents related to its Epstein probe. On Wednesday, Black sued Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif., who is poised to become chair of the Oversight Committee in the next Congress, alleging Garcia defamed him in statements regarding Epstein. The lawsuit focuses on Garcia's claims in a TV interview that Black "is at the center of Jeffrey Epstein's crimes" and "was one of the last people to actually interact" with Epstein before his death, among others. The Department of Justice's mountain of files related to Epstein became a major focus in late 2025 and early 2026, after Congress passed a bill ordering the DOJ to make those records public. Trump's name is referenced thousands of times in the files that have been released.
